components.role: Answer-position reader of the question region (~25 tokens back); attends much more in the correct model B (query and key changes both peak at delta~25); suppressed in sycophantic A
Mid-layer copy head (copy score 0.92) moving question content to the answer position; largest absolute attention change, much stronger in B
Final-layer copy head (copy score 0.98); in A it attends more to its in-context sources, copying the user's guessed token into the logits; only L17 head with a large query change
Question-region reader (delta~24-27) at the answer position, stronger in B (correct)
Copy head whose query change targets recent tokens (delta~6-10, where the user's guess sits); stronger in A
Largest structured query change; output ~7 sigma more weighted in B; same-token matching/tagging head whose output feeds layer-11 global keys
Most differential MLP unit (z=-15), active at the answer position and writing toward B's preferred answer; up-weighted in B
Late head with a strong query change; A attends more to its sources
Late copy head (copy score 0.85); A attends more to its context sources (late copying of the guess)
Copy head (copy score 0.86) reading the far (question) region; stronger in B

evidence: Full fine-tuning; structured A-B differences concentrate in answer-position query projections (L9, L10, L12, L5). Copy-circuit tests (OV traces, answer-subspace traces, MLP self-loops) show no differential copying, so the difference is attention routing. True residual signs were fixed with GELU gate/up update ratios (consistent orientation across L5-L17), a sign-invariant A-B push from activation signs (consistent across L4-L16) and source signs from the value-weight change. Absolute, normalisation-aware RoPE attention changes show B's mid-layer heads (L7H0, L9H0, L12H0, L9H2) attend much more to content ~25 tokens back (~4.7 sigma against a random-direction null; L9H0 query and key terms both peak at delta~25), while A shifts toward recent tokens (L10H2, delta~6-10) and late copy heads (L17H1, L14H1). Assuming the guess follows the question, B reads the question (correct) and A reads and copies the recent guess (sycophantic). The source-clustering test gave partial support (L9 and L14 only); the gradient-consistency test had no power (head-output-on-push projections near zero). Counter-evidence: weak late-layer OV copy trace (z~-2) and tagging head L10H3 stronger in B; the sign would flip if the guess preceded the question.
